title: prdr-yagni contract data
description: Reference schema (FAFF-256, extended FAFF-815). The SHAPE of the PRDR UPPER (YAGNI / value) gate verdict that `faff prdr yagni` PRODUCES and `faff contract prdr-yagni` VALIDATES (consumer-side conformance, mirroring prd-readiness / prdr-admission). It is 255's `upper: {admit, reason}` verdict, plus the two-phase audit trail (the deterministic trace-to-goal precondition, the methodology proposal, the adversarial challenge) and FAFF-815's three-goal-set model: `cited_goals` (C — the PRDR's cited set, widened to C∪V on an under-citation admit), `dod_covers` (V — the goals the DoD covers), and `over_scope` (V⊄D — the deterministic gold-plating signal). NO safe coerce target — faff's own producer emits it, so an out-of-enum proposal.verdict is a fail-loud, never coerced toward `admit`; the gate is fail-safe toward REFUSAL. The load-bearing invariant (an `admit` implies trace_to_goal ∧ proposal.verdict==admit ∧ challenge.ran ∧ ¬over_scope ∧ (¬challenge.overturns ∨ (under-citation ∧ challenge.ground==over-scope)) — 'no gold-plating on doubt', admitting only a mis-attributed over-scope under-citation) is enforced in code as a conformance violation; it is not expressible in this shape schema. `challenge.ground` is the closed-vocab overturn reason (over-scope|unserved|other; absent ⇒ other, fail-safe) that gates the under-citation admit (Q7). Grounding is advisory: `grounding_present` is shape-checked but never gate-decisive.
